ph: Welcomed with a garland of flowers, 10 Oct 99

w: Swamishri performed the ground breaking ceremony for a new mandir at Absecon Town.

During Swamishri's morning puja music artistes of Kachchh, traditionally attired, sang and played a variety of local instruments like the morchang, bhorindo, jodiyo pavo, ravan hathho, matlu-tagaru, etc. Swamishri blessed all the artistes.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Nar Narayan Dev, Guru Parampara, Shri Hanumanji and Shri Ganapatiji at the mandir in Bhuj. Thereafter, Swamishri blessed the murti-pratishtha assembly.
At 5.00 p.m., Swamishri departed from Bhuj and arrived in Mandvi at 6.30 p.m. A satsang assembly was held in Mandvi.

The main evening assembly stage to commemorate Gunatitanand Swami's birthday festival was decorated with an impressive 52 ft high and 40 ft wide replica of Akshar Deri. The assembly commenced at 8.00 p.m. The entire celebration was interspersed with five artis, two dramas - Transformation of Valera Varu and Uga Khuman traditional dances, inauguration of Swaminarayan Bal Prakash (colour, English edition) and honoring of Swamishri with garlands. The assembly concluded at 11.30 p.m.
Swamishri's vicharan in Mombasa At 11.45 am Swamishri arrived in Mombasa by plane from Dar-es-Salaam. The evening welcome assembly was held in the Hindu Shivalay Mandir.

At 12.00 noon Shri Vamdeva Shastri (David Frawley), a scholar in Hinduism, met Swamishri. He had written a 175 page book on Hinduism for the BAPS Sanstha. He said, “There is no spiritual element in Delhi. The creation of Akshardham here will change the atmosphere in Delhi. It will transform the minds of people. The complex will create a tremendous atmosphere in Delhi and it will bridge the past with the future. Through this complex there will be the realization of pride for India among young children. This place will become a seat of knowledge and study for all.”

At 10.00 am the Vice CEO of Hewlett Packard, Shri Vyomesh Joshi, Financial Controller John and Industrial Psychologist Frank met Swamishri. Frank said, “I am incredibly impressed in many, many different ways. And one of the things is to hear that the whole development was made in five years and the major part in two years, all by volunteers. I look around and I see everybody happy. Vyomesh Joshi, Vice CEO, said, “I am really impressed with what I saw, not only the dedication and the work 11,000 volunteers have done, but when you walk in you are just awed by the whole complex. The details in making Akshardham are amazing. When you go in and see all the ceilings and carvings that have been done and then I think you see dedication and the love and I was just absolutely awed. ”

Children of The Swaminarayan School enjoyed a special evening with Pramukh Swami Maharaj at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. The event included a variety of cultural presentations from students, namely, instrumental performances, speeches, dances, recital of shloks and bhajans. Viveksagar Swami spoke about the history of The Swaminarayan School and the importance of the Mandir and School in providing education and values. Swamishri gave awards to high-achievers in the GCSE examinations.

Thereafter Professor Gavin Flood, Academic Director for Hindu Studies from Oxford University, encouraged Hindu children to pursue Hindu Studies and become an intellectual voice for the Hindu faith in his address.

Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly and praised the preparation and presentations of the students. He thanked the parents and teachers for developing talent in their children and underlined the importance of nurturing children from infancy to allow them to develop moral and spiritual values, so they could serve society and their parents. Swamishri also blessed the MP for Brent North Hon. Barry Gardiner who passed an Early Day Motion (EDM 2038) in the Parliament to mark the BAPS Centenary and the visit of Swamishri to the UK on 8 October 2007 with the signatures of seven MPs. Mr Barry Gardiner was inspired to do this because he wished to inform all about the worldwide activities of BAPS for the service and betterment of humanity. Similarly, the MP for Brent South Hon. Dawn Butler also passed an EDM 2049 on 8 October 2007 with signatures of 11 MPs.

st.t: BAPS News – Swaminarayan School Din – Wednesday 10 October 2007
w: The children of The Swaminarayan School enjoyed a special evening with Pramukh Swami Maharaj on Wednesday 10 October 2007. The event, held at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London, involved a variety of cultural performances from students of the school including musical pieces, speeches, shlokas and bhajans. Dressed in their uniforms, the pupils delighted the audience with great displays of talent, underlining the variety of activities that the establishment develops.

Viveksagar Swami spoke of the history of the Swaminarayan School and the importance of the Mandir and School as a provider of education and values. An awards ceremony for high-achievers in the GCSE examinations this year took place. The presentations from the students also included a tabla ensemble and recitation of Sanskrit shlokas. The pupils of Year 6 also entertained the audience with a dance.

Professor Gavin Flood, Academic Director for Hindu Studies from Oxford University, and the tutor of Paramtattva Swami, was also present in the programme. In his address, Professor Flood encouraged Hindu children to pursue Hindu Studies and become an intellectual voice for the Hindu faith.

Swamishri blessed the assembly and praised the preparation of the children in their performances. He thanked the parents and teachers for developing talent in their children and underlined the importance of nurturing children from infancy to allow them to develop moral and spiritual values, so they could serve society and their parents.

During Swamishri’s stay in Junagadh children and youths briefly celebrated various festivals each day on the mandir premises when Swamishri came for Thakorji’s darshan. They celebrated Shivratri, Yogi Jayanti, Guru Purnima, Raksha Bandhan, Janmashtmi, Ganesh Chaturthi, Vijaya Dashmi, Chopda Pujan, Diwali and Swamishri’s birthday.
Today, in Swamishri’s puja, BAPS children sang kirtans, performed a traditional dance, delivered a speech and recitation of shlokas from the 15th Chapter of the Bhagvad Gita.

In the evening assembly kishores presented dramas on ‘Upasana’ and ‘Ten Fools’. Thereafter Swamishri was honoured with garlands. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the assembly saying, “Junagadh is a land of enlightened rishis. Bhagwan Swaminarayan came here as Nilkanth Varni. Gunatitanand Swami was appointed as the Mahant of the Mandir and he and his sadhus toured the region to spread the knowledge of Akshar and Purushottam.” Swamishri also explained that our true form is atma, and as long as we believe ourselves to be the body we will experience misery and pain. The Gunatit Sadhu is the doorway to moksha.
A hydraulic lift has been arranged so that Pramukh Swami Maharaj can go up into the mandir. When Swamishri goes up into the mandir by that hydraulic lift, the youths below present various programmes.

Today it was the children's turn. Of the children who had come from Porbandar, two had dressed up as Gandhiji and Sudama. Swamishri's eyes fell on these two children. Humbly Swamishri said to the child dressed as Gandhiji, "Gandhiji! Please say Jai Swaminarayan." At the very moment Swamishri was saying this, I also said, "Gandhiji! Say Jai Swaminarayan." On one hand, Swamishri addressed even a small child with a respectful word, because he saw Gandhiji in him too. While I, seeing only the child's outward form, addressed him in a casual, belittling way. How refined and discerning Swamishri is!!
Kikani Saheb, the retired Vice Chancellor of the Agricultural University, had come for darshan. One of Kikani Saheb's three sons said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "I have a question."
Swamishri said, "Ask."

He said, "I recently read the book 'Prasangam'. In one incident in it, you said, 'The pony is weak, but the rider is fresh.' So please bless us that we too may understand the difference between these two."
Swamishri was pleased with such a question, asked with the spirit of a true seeker, and said, "This will come through the company of the Sant."
While Pramukh Swami Maharaj was doing his puja, a blind boy named Shyam Bharadva gave a speech with great energy and enthusiasm on the topic "Recognise with the inner eye".

During the meetings, this boy came for Swamishri's darshan. As soon as he saw him, Swamishri said, "It is good that you have come. During the puja I wished that you would come." Having said this, with eyes moist with compassion he said, "How did you learn to give speeches?"
He said, "My brother and my mother taught me."
Pleased, Swamishri said, "Good, good. Just keep progressing like this."

A hydraulic lift has been arranged so that Pramukh Swami Maharaj can go up into the mandir. When Swamishri goes up into the mandir by that hydraulic lift, the youths present different programmes below.

Today it was the children's turn. Of the children who had come from Porbandar, two had dressed up as Gandhiji and Sudama. Swamishri's eyes fell on these two children. Humbly, Swamishri said to the child dressed as Gandhiji, "Gandhiji! Please say Jai Swaminarayan." At the very moment Swamishri was saying this, I too said, "Gandhiji! Say Jai Swaminarayan." On one side, Swamishri was addressing even a small child respectfully, because he saw Gandhiji in him too. Whereas I, looking only at the child's outer form, addressed him casually. How courteous Swamishri is!!
Kikani sahib, retired Vice Chancellor of the Agricultural University, had come for darshan. One of Kikani sahib's three sons said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "I have a question."
Swamishri said, "Ask."
He said, "I recently read the book 'Prasangam'. In one incident in it you said, 'The pony is weak, but the rider is fresh.' Please bless us so that we too understand the difference between the two."
Swamishri was pleased with his question, asked with the feeling of a seeker, and said, "This will happen through the company of sants."
While Pramukh Swami Maharaj was doing his puja, a blind boy named Shyam Bhardva gave a very spirited and joyful speech on the subject "Recognise with the inner eye".

This boy came for Swamishri's darshan during the meetings. As soon as he saw him, Swamishri said, "It is good that you came. During the puja I had wished that you would come." Having said this, with eyes moist with compassion, he said, "How did you learn to speak like that?"
He said, "My brother and my mother taught me."
Pleased, Swamishri said, "Good, good. Just keep progressing like this."
When Mahant Swami Maharaj returned to his room after walking, Miteshbhai Kolorama came bringing his young child, Gunsagar. Gunsagar asked Swamishri, "How does it feel like to be a Guru?"
Swamishri laughed and said, "Offer devotion with das bhav (the attitude of a servant). I enjoy das bhav!"
Oh! The guru of all regards himself as the servant of all, and finds joy in it!
Showering blessings in the evening assembly, Mahant Swami Maharaj said:

"From Bhagwan Swaminarayan onwards, the gurus have spoken about removing dislike and fault-finding as no one else has. In this, the gain is in crores (if we do not see faults), and the loss is also in crores! So be careful. One does not look at one's own nature, however crooked it may be, but looks at 'this one is like this and that one is like that.' But what are you like?
Pramukh Swami Maharaj used to say, 'Seeing faults is like running a 100 ton roller over yourself.'
Yogibapa used to say, 'That is the path of eating poison.'
So for us that path is closed. There is much else to see. A person has many virtues; if he had no virtues, he would not be in this Satsang.
There are two choices: sing praises of virtues and go to Akshardham, or sing of faults and stay outside Akshardham. What will you choose?" (Everyone said together, "Akshardham.")

"When we go to buy vegetables, we pick good aubergines and potatoes. So everyone has good virtues; shouldn't we take only those virtues? In everything we take the good, yet when it comes to dislike and faults we collect rubbish. But what do we need it for? What is the need to see dislike and faults? Why? Shouldn't we see virtues?"
